Subject: Order Form + Exhibit B redline (stair-step discounts / true-up)

Sergio — attaching our redline of Exhibit B and the order form. A few items we flagged that need clarification before procurement can sign: 

1) Stair-step discount tiers (Section 2): your team included a 3-tier schedule with increasing discounts at volume thresholds. We need a clearer definition of "monthly committed usage" vs "billable usage" to avoid disputes at month-end.

2) True-up cadence (Section 5): Olive prefers quarterly true-ups for usage reconciliation. Your original draft said "annual true-up" — that creates material cashflow uncertainty for us.

3) Price-protection / floor (Section 6): we redlined a price floor clause that prevents price increases during the first 12 months. Can Redwood provide a limited carve that preserves your right to increase for external cost changes (e.g., cloud provider pass-throughs)?

We also called out a request for an explicit credit cap (so we don't accrue open credit liabilities) and a one-off transition credit for our first 30 days.

See attached: OLV_ExhibitB_redline_v2.pdf and OrderForm_OLV-042_marked.docx.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call tomorrow if that helps.

—Daniel
Daniel Kim
Procurement Manager, Olive Tech

Daniel — thanks for the clear redline and the summary. High level responses below and then I copied legal/finance for specific language: 

- Definitions: agree we need to explicitly define "billable usage" (we're proposing billed tokens + embeddings). I'll attach a short definition insert for Exhibit B.

- True-up cadence: we can accept quarterly true-ups for the first 12 months as a commercial concession, but we need a firm cap on the maximum credit Redwood would owe in any true-up period (finance asked for a "credit liability ceiling"). Marcus — can you confirm a quantifiable cap we can offer (percent of monthly committed revenue)?

- Price floor / protection: Redwood can limit price increases for the first 12 months except for documented third-party pass-throughs. We want to avoid an absolute floor that prevents reasonable adjustments. Laura — propose fallback language for Section 6.

- Transition credit: happy to provide a one-time stability credit (applied to first invoice) in exchange for a 12-month minimum committed spend.

I've attached our internal suggestions as a draft markup — see OrderForm_OLV-042_marked.docx. If Daniel is available, let's do a quick 30-minute sync Monday to finalize redlines.

Onward,
Sergio
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Order Form + Exhibit B redline (stair-step discounts / true-up)

Team — I reviewed Olive's redlines and Sergio's commercial responses. Proposed legal edits below (included as tracked-change snippets in the internal copy). Key points: 

1) BILLABLE USAGE DEFINITION: Insert new definition into Exhibit B: 
"Billable Usage" means the aggregate of (a) generated tokens consumed by Customer requests; (b) embedding units consumed by Customer requests; and (c) data processing fees as listed in the Order Form, excluding tokens used for model pre-warm operations initiated by Redwood.

2) TRUE-UP / CREDIT LIABILITY CAP (Section 5): We can accept quarterly true-ups for Year 1. Proposed cap: Redwood's cumulative credit obligation for any single true-up period will not exceed 25% of the Customer's committed monthly spend for that period. This protects Redwood from open-ended liability while providing Olive with more frequent reconciliation.

3) PRICE ADJUSTMENTS (Section 6): Replace Olive's absolute floor with the following compromise: 
"Redwood will not unilaterally increase unit prices for services during the 12-month Initial Term except to reflect (a) increases in third-party costs (evidenced by written documentation), (b) changes in applicable taxes or duties, or (c) agreed upgrades to service levels. Any adjustment shall not exceed 10% in a rolling 12-month period and Customer shall be provided 30 days' notice."

4) TRANSITION/STABILITY CREDIT: We can offer a one-time credit equal to 5% of the first monthly invoice, applied automatically if Customer meets the 12-month committed spend.

Marcus — please confirm the 25% cap and the 5% credit are acceptable from a finance/levers perspective. Sergio — if Olive pushes for quarterly true-ups beyond Year 1, we should ask for additional margin protection.

I'll prepare a clean redline with these edits and a DocuSign envelope once commercial signs off.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks Sergio and Laura — appreciate the constructive compromise. A few quick asks from Olive: 

• The 25% credit cap looks reasonable — can you add an example calculation in the Annex so our auditors can reconcile easily?

• Regarding the 10% rolling cap on increases: Olive asks for a carve that any increase tied exclusively to a new premium feature rollout (not third-party costs) be limited to a separate optional add-on that must be agreed in writing. In other words, no surprise baseline feature charge increases under the Exhibit B mechanism.

• Transition credit: Olive accepts the 5% credit tied to the 12-month commitment, but asks that the credit be applied as an invoice line item (not an off-ledger waiver) for our accounting treatment.

If Redwood can add the example calculation and the invoice-line application of the credit, we can remove open redlines and push to signature. We'll await Marcus' confirmation on the cap and the invoice format.

If needed, I'm available Tuesday morning for a short call to finalize.

Best,
Daniel
